name: L-tetrahydropalmatine (l-THP)
short: Children: life-threatening slow heart rate, with depressed breathing, after swallowing a Chinese herbal tablet one abstract says contains l-THP (case reports). Adults: hepatitis after long-term use.
text: The serious harms come from case reports of a Chinese herbal tablet product (named in the sources) that a 1996 case series says contains levo-tetrahydropalmatine; that series also says the product's constituents are misidentified on the package. In that series of three children and three adults, a single acute ingestion in children rapidly produced life-threatening neurological and cardiovascular effects, while long-term use in adults was associated with hepatitis; a 1993 public-health report describes three children who developed life-threatening slow heart rate (bradycardia) with central nervous system and breathing depression after swallowing the tablets (the abstracts do not say whether these are the same children). A 1994 case series of seven previously healthy patients who took the same product (this abstract gives the plant name Lycopodium serratum in brackets after the product name) describes acute hepatitis after a mean of 20 weeks, with fever, fatigue, nausea, itching, abdominal pain, jaundice and an enlarged liver; it resolved in six patients within a mean of 8 weeks, and taking the product again caused abrupt recurrence of hepatitis in two patients; this abstract does not itself name l-THP. In randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials of l-THP itself taken by mouth, a 4-day study in 24 adult men who used cocaine found it safe and well tolerated, with no significant differences from placebo in the number of side effects, heart rate, blood pressure, blood counts or ECG; and a 4-week study in 63 adults with schizophrenia taking stable antipsychotic medicine found it well tolerated, with fewer extrapyramidal (movement) symptoms, but it raised two inflammatory markers (soluble intercellular adhesion molecule 1 and CRP) compared with placebo. Interactions: in the cocaine study, l-THP did not affect the blood levels of cocaine or its acute cardiovascular effects; no other interaction data were found in the cited sources.
